title: Cardi B, Travis Scott Set For 'GTA VI' Takeover Of Popular Miami Strip Club

 By Tony M. Centeno
 November 13, 2026
 Photo: Amanda Barona for Booby Trap On The River Cardi B and Travis Scott are heading down to Miami to help bring Vice City to life in celebration of the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI. 
On Wednesday night, November 11, Booby Trap On The River announced that the Bronx bombshell will take over the popular strip club next week on the eve of GTA VI's debut. Cardi B is expected to host the event with some surprise guests, and she'll also hit the stage for a special performance of her song "Don't Chart." The song appears on the official GTA VI soundtrack alongside other major artists, including Travis Scott , Future , Metro Boomin , and more. 
 Photo: Booby Trap On The River & Rockstar Games The after-party continues at Booby Trap following Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival in Wynwood. Scott will host the official after-party after he and Bardi perform at Rockstar Games' first music festival in Miami. Don Toliver , Kodak Black , SoFaygo , Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso , Metro Boomin , Tainy , Rauw Alejandro , and others are also expected to hit the stage. The event is going down Saturday, November 21, at Mana Wynwood. 
Booby Trap On The River is leading the charge to bring the coveted video game to life in Miami. Since the rollout for the video game began, numerous hotspots in Miami-Dade County have been transformed to fit the aesthetic of Vice City, including the Kaseya Center which was decked out in signage from the game and multiple tricked-out cars that paraded down South Beach. Rupert Humphries, senior vice president of narrative at Rockstar, told DAZED that Bobby Trap specifically played a role in establishing Miami's hip-hop scene in Vice City. 
"We were also really interested in how the hip-hop scene in Miami exists in house parties in Overtown, clubs like Booby Trap on the River, and then high-end places on South Beach where bottles can cost thousands of dollars," Humphries said. "We needed characters who could take us through those worlds.”
